symbols.name: set of triples
symbols.meaning: The set of all three-element subsets of the ground set $[h]$.
symbols.quote: A *triple* is a three-element subset of $[h]$, and $\mathcal T$ denotes the set of all triples.

symbols.name: bank X
symbols.meaning: One of the two banks of scalars, with entries $X_\tau$ indexed by triples of triples.
symbols.quote: The network has two banks, $X$ and $Y$, with entries $X_\tau$ and $Y_\tau$.

symbols.name: bank Y
symbols.meaning: The second of the two banks of scalars, with entries $Y_\tau$.
symbols.quote: The network has two banks, $X$ and $Y$, with entries $X_\tau$ and $Y_\tau$.

symbols.name: bank index
symbols.meaning: A triple of triples, indexing the entries of a bank.
symbols.quote: A *bank* is a family of scalars indexed by $\tau=(\tau_1,\tau_2,\tau_3)\in\mathcal T^3$.

symbols.name: source vector
symbols.meaning: The vector of one bank's entries along the varying coordinate, read by a forward invocation.
symbols.quote: Call these two vectors $\xi$ (the source) and $\eta$ (the target), so that $\xi_T$ and $\eta_S$ are their entries.

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.meaning: The vector of the other bank's entries along the varying coordinate, updated by a forward invocation.
symbols.quote: Call these two vectors $\xi$ (the source) and $\eta$ (the target), so that $\xi_T$ and $\eta_S$ are their entries.

symbols.name: side wire
symbols.meaning: The scratch wire for an ordered pair of neighbouring triples $(S,T)$.
symbols.quote: For each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ there is a side wire $W_{ST}$.

symbols.name: central wire
symbols.meaning: The scratch wire attached to an element $\ell$ of the ground set.
symbols.quote: For each $\ell\in[h]$ there is a central wire $C_\ell$, where $\ell$ is an element of $[h]$ here.

symbols.name: ground element
symbols.meaning: An element of the ground set $[h]$, whose central wire is $C_\ell$.
symbols.quote: For each $\ell\in[h]$ there is a central wire $C_\ell$, where $\ell$ is an element of $[h]$ here.

symbols.name: vector of E
symbols.meaning: A vector of the ambient space $E=\mathbb Q^h$, an argument of the bit network form.
symbols.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\delta,\delta'\rangle=\delta^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\delta'$, where $\delta,\delta'$ are vectors of $E$, $I$ is the identity matrix and $J$ the all-ones matrix.

symbols.name: larger label
symbols.meaning: The larger of the two nested labels on an edge, which contains the smaller label $U$.
symbols.quote: Write $U'$ for the larger label of an edge and $U$ for the smaller.

relations.predicate: labels its gates and terminals with
relations.quote: The network labels its gates and terminals with [Subspace labels](subspace-labels.md): nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space $E$.

relations.predicate: is built within the framework of
relations.quote: The network is built within the framework of [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md): each wire is a role, and each gate carries a frame, so the same scalar gates can act on arrays.
Orthogonality and nondegeneracy are tested with the form of [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md).
The network checks nondegeneracy through [Eigenvalue](eigenvalue.md)s of its form matrix $I-J/9$.
